name: Tanzania
summary: The Serengeti and the Ngorongoro crater, the highest mountain in Africa, and a spice island with a thousand-year-old stone town on it.
window_alt: A footpath through flat-topped acacia below a snow-capped volcano
when: Calving on the southern Serengeti in February; the crossings run June to October.

entries.caption: Into the Wild
entries.description: The Serengeti runs unbroken to the horizon, and the migration has been circling it far longer than anyone has watched.
entries.subject: the endless short-grass plains of the Serengeti at sunrise

entries.caption: The Ngorongoro Crater
entries.description: A collapsed caldera twenty kilometres across with its own permanent population of thirty thousand animals.
entries.subject: the floor of the Ngorongoro Crater seen from the rim

entries.caption: The Big Five, and Then Some
entries.description: Lion, leopard, elephant, buffalo and rhino, plus the largest elephant herds left in East Africa.
entries.subject: a lion pride resting on a kopje in the Serengeti

entries.caption: Following the Migration
entries.description: Calving on the southern plains in February, the Grumeti in June, the Mara river in August — the circuit never stops.
entries.subject: wildebeest herds streaming across the Serengeti plains

entries.caption: Kilimanjaro, 5,895 m
entries.description: The highest free-standing mountain on earth: rainforest, moorland, alpine desert and glacier in five days of walking.
entries.subject: the snow-capped summit of Kilimanjaro above the cloud line
entries.photo_alt: The snow-capped summit of Kilimanjaro rising clear above a thick bank of cloud, with a single elephant crossing the plain far below it

entries.caption: Materuni, Under Kilimanjaro
entries.description: Eighty metres of cold water through Chagga coffee farms on the lower slopes, an easy walk from Moshi.
entries.subject: the Materuni waterfall in the forest below Kilimanjaro

entries.caption: Manyara and the Rufiji
entries.description: Flamingo and tree-climbing lions at Manyara; the Rufiji braiding through Nyerere, the largest park in Africa.
entries.subject: the Rufiji river braiding through Nyerere National Park

entries.caption: Zanzibar, Nungwi to Paje
entries.description: White sand, warm shallow water and dhows still built by hand on the beach at Nungwi.
entries.subject: white sand and traditional dhows on the beach at Nungwi, Zanzibar

entries.caption: Udzungwa and Jozani
entries.description: The Udzungwa scarp holds species found nowhere else; Jozani holds the red colobus, also found nowhere else.
entries.subject: a Zanzibar red colobus monkey in Jozani Forest

entries.caption: Uhuru Peak by Machame
entries.description: Six days up the Machame route, one very long night to the summit, and a sunrise you have to earn.
entries.subject: trekkers on the Machame route high on Kilimanjaro

entries.caption: Maasai, Chagga, Swahili
entries.description: Cattle-keepers on the northern plains, coffee farmers on the mountain, and a coast that has always faced east.
entries.subject: Maasai men in ceremonial dress on the northern Tanzanian plains

entries.caption: The Hadzabe of Lake Eyasi
entries.description: One of the last hunter-gatherer peoples in Africa, speaking a click language unrelated to anything nearby.
entries.subject: a Hadzabe hunter with a bow near Lake Eyasi

entries.caption: Spice, Ugali, Urojo
entries.description: Cloves and cardamom from the Zanzibar plantations, grilled seafood at Forodhani, and ugali everywhere else.
entries.subject: grilled seafood stalls at Forodhani Gardens in Stone Town

entries.caption: Sauti za Busara
entries.description: Four days of live music from across the continent inside the old Arab fort in Stone Town, every February.
entries.subject: musicians performing at the Sauti za Busara festival in Stone Town

entries.caption: Tingatinga and Makonde
entries.description: Enamel-bright Tingatinga painting from Dar es Salaam, and Makonde ebony carving from the southern plateau.
entries.subject: a Makonde carver working ebony wood

entries.caption: Stone Town and Kilwa
entries.description: Stone Town is UNESCO-listed; Kilwa Kisiwani was the richest port on the Swahili coast six centuries ago.
entries.subject: the ruins of the great mosque at Kilwa Kisiwani

entries.caption: Olduvai and the Coast
entries.description: Olduvai Gorge holds the earliest human record; the coast holds a thousand years of Indian Ocean trade.
entries.subject: the layered walls of Olduvai Gorge in the Ngorongoro conservation area

entries.caption: Dar es Salaam
entries.description: Harbour of peace: the ferry terminal, the fish market at Kivukoni, and the dhows still working the channel.
entries.subject: the harbour and skyline of Dar es Salaam from the water

entries.caption: The Doors of Stone Town
entries.description: Brass-studded Indian doors and carved Omani frames, on coral-rag houses in alleys too narrow to drive.
entries.subject: a brass-studded carved door in a Stone Town alley, Zanzibar

entries.caption: Dala Dalas and Dhows
entries.description: Minibuses inland, dhows on the water, and a fish auction at Kivukoni that starts before it is light.
entries.subject: the early morning fish market at Kivukoni in Dar es Salaam

entries.caption: Boma and Coffee Farm
entries.description: Maasai boma visits on the crater rim road, and Chagga coffee walks on the lower slopes of Kilimanjaro.
entries.subject: a Chagga family roasting coffee on a farm below Kilimanjaro

entries.caption: Snorkelling Mnemba
entries.description: The atoll off the northeast tip of Zanzibar, plus kite surfing at Paje and diving at Pemba.
entries.subject: snorkelling over coral reef at Mnemba atoll, Zanzibar

entries.caption: Camps and Spice Islands
entries.description: Mobile camps that follow the migration, and beach houses on the Zanzibar east coast with nothing either side.
entries.subject: a luxury tented camp on the Serengeti plains at dusk

entries.caption: Ngorongoro, Shared Ground
entries.description: The conservation area is the rare model where Maasai pastoralists and wildlife legally use the same land.
entries.subject: Maasai herders and cattle on the Ngorongoro conservation area highlands

entries.caption: Acacia, Kopje, Sunset
entries.description: The Serengeti kopjes at the end of the day, and the migration column stretching past the edge of the frame.
entries.subject: an acacia silhouetted against the Serengeti sunset

entries.caption: Ruaha and Katavi
entries.description: The south and west: huge elephant populations, hippo crowded into shrinking pools, and no other vehicles.
entries.subject: elephants beneath baobabs in Ruaha National Park

entries.caption: Mountain, Plain and Reef
entries.description: Summit Africa's highest mountain, cross the Serengeti and sleep on the Indian Ocean, in the same fortnight.
entries.subject: Kilimanjaro rising above the acacia plains at sunrise
